tagline: Nyhavn's colored houses, Tivoli's 1843 amusement park and the world's best restaurants — all reached by bicycle.
overview: Copenhagen is the template for the livable city: more bicycles than people, harbour water clean enough to swim in, and a food scene that produced Noma and a wave of New Nordic restaurants.

The postcard is Nyhavn — the 17th-century canal of painted townhouses where Hans Christian Andersen wrote his tales. Tivoli Gardens, the 1843 amusement park in the city centre, inspired Walt Disney; the Little Mermaid sits modestly on her rock; and freetown Christiania keeps its anarchist commune vibe going after 50 years.

Speed's 2024 tour streamed from Copenhagen. The city also runs Amager Bakke — a power plant with a ski slope on its roof — and the Round Tower's spiral ramp, climbed by horse-drawn carriages for centuries.
